stories.headline: Massive Himalayan floods kill hundreds across Nepal and Tibet
stories.body:
Floods caused by a glacier collapse killed hundreds of people across Nepal and Tibet [c1, c12]. As of Sunday, 810 people died in the disaster [c1]. Nepalese authorities counted 794 dead in Nepal [c1]. Chinese authorities reported 16 dead in Tibet [c1]. NDTV reported a different count of 734 recovered bodies [c12]. Search teams reported 3,048 people missing across both regions [c2]. In Nepal, 2,502 people remain missing [c2]. In Tibet, 546 people are missing [c2].

Nepal's disaster management authority NDRRMA said 933 workers from hydropower projects are untraced [c3]. The Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal listed 537 project workers as unaccounted for [c3]. The Nepalese Army used helicopters to airlift heavy earth-moving machinery [c4]. Machinery went to the Upper Trishuli-3A hydropower project [c4]. Rescuers needed to reach a mud-filled entry point of a tunnel [c4]. Army spokesperson Brig Gen Rajaram Basnet said rescuers found the crown head of Trishuli 3A [c5]. Teams dug a hole into the tunnel to search for survivors inside [c5].

India's Ministry of External Affairs said rescuers saved 149 Indian nationals in Nepal [c6]. Another 275 Indian citizens remain missing in Nepal [c6]. Chinese authorities said 546 people were missing in Gyirong in Tibet [c7]. That number included 261 foreign citizens from 23 countries [c7]. Among those missing in Gyirong were 49 Indians and 104 Nepalese citizens [c7].

India sent four relief flights carrying 68.5 tonnes of supplies to Kathmandu [c8]. India also sent a 13-member army tunnel-rescue team to Nepal [c8]. Six forensic teams from India joined the relief efforts [c8]. Recovering from the disaster could cost one-tenth of Nepal's annual economic output [c10].

Officials and experts from Nepal and China met in Kathmandu on May 27 [c9]. They discussed monitoring floods, weather hazards, and glacier threats [c9]. Twelve days before the disaster, China's World Meteorological Centre emailed Nepal [c11]. The centre warned of a monsoon depression [c11]. It also warned of potential flash floods between August 14 and 19 [c11].

vocab.meaning: a large mass of ice that moves slowly over land
related to scientific tests used to solve crimes or investigate deaths

stories.headline: US military strikes Iranian rocket launchers in Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
The US military struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on August 30 [c13]. US Central Command spokesman Cdr Tim Hawkins said Iranian forces prepared to launch rockets [c17]. The rockets carried sea mines intended for the Strait of Hormuz [c17]. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi called the strike a strategic mistake [c18]. Mohebbi promised economic and military consequences for the US [c18]. Iran's Tasnim news agency said the drone strike killed two people and injured two others [c19].

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a projectile struck an oil tanker north of Khasab on August 29 [c16]. A US source reported that Iran launched missiles at US forces in Jordan [c22]. All incoming missiles were intercepted [c22]. The US and Israel started strikes on Iran on February 28, beginning a six-month war [c20]. Eighteen US service members have died during the war [c21]. Iranian officials said Iran lost about $270 billion in economic damage [c15].

Normally, about 20% of global oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz [c14]. President Donald Trump said 24 commercial ships passed through recently [c23]. Before the war, about 130 ships passed through daily [c23]. The US military redirected 83 commercial ships and disabled three as part of a blockade [c24].

vocab.meaning: the closing off of a area to prevent people or goods from entering or leaving
stopped or caught before reaching a destination

stories.headline: US and Venezuela sign 25-year oil deal to refill US reserves
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced a new oil agreement with Venezuela to refill the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve [c25]. Trump described the deal as the biggest oil deal in world history [c30]. On August 21, the US reserve held about 290 million barrels [c26]. That level was near a 44-year low [c26]. The deal follows the US capture of former President Nicolás Maduro in January on drug charges [c29].

Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the 25-year energy deal covers 17 strategic oilfields [c27]. Rodríguez said the deal targets production over 1.5 million barrels per day [c27]. The agreement involves about 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves [c35]. Rodríguez estimated the deal could generate $209 billion in revenue based on $65 per barrel [c28]. About $19 per barrel will go directly to Venezuela [c28].

A US official said a new company received 100-year rights to untapped Venezuelan oilfields [c31]. The company involves the US government and an unnamed private operator [c31]. It gives the US 55% of effective output [c31]. US Senator Tim Kaine called the deal corrupt [c32]. Former PDVSA head Rafael Ramírez accused the administration of betraying the homeland [c33]. Protesters marched in Caracas against foreign control [c34].

vocab.meaning: money that a business or government receives

stories.headline: Icelandic voters reject proposal to restart EU membership talks
stories.body:
Icelandic voters rejected a proposal to restart talks to join the European Union in a national referendum [c36]. Results showed 52.8% voted against resuming talks, while 47.2% voted in favor [c36]. The BBC reported a margin of about 12,600 votes out of over 225,000 cast [c36]. France 24 reported that around 9,500 votes separated the two sides [c44]. Voter turnout reached 82.5%, the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009 [c37].

Iceland first applied to join the EU in 2009 after a banking collapse [c38]. Talks were put on hold in 2013 [c38]. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir said her government will not revisit EU membership [c40]. Frostadóttir previously said Iceland already follows 75% of EU rules [c47]. Capital city voters supported joining the EU, while rural regions voted against [c41]. Fish and marine industries make up nearly 40% of Iceland's exports [c39]. AFP reported that about 90% of fisheries companies opposed EU membership [c45]. Iceland fought the Cod Wars over fishing rights with Britain in the 1970s [c46]. European Council President António Costa said the EU respects the choice [c43]. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage congratulated voters for keeping their independence [c42].

vocab.meaning: a direct vote by the public on a single political question
the act of joining an organization or alliance

stories.headline: NASA launches Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard SpaceX rocket
stories.body:
NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX rocket on August 30 [c48]. SpaceX launched the $4.3 billion telescope from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida using a Falcon Heavy rocket [c48, c54]. The space telescope reached orbit 10 minutes after liftoff [c57]. It is traveling on a 100-day journey to Lagrange Point 2 [c50, c55]. That point is located about 1 million miles, or 1.6 million kilometers, from Earth [c50, c55]. The telescope will join the James Webb Space Telescope at that location [c55].

The telescope is named after physicist Nancy Grace Roman [c52]. She served as NASA's first chief astronomer in the 1960s and its first female executive [c52]. The telescope features a field of vision 100 times larger than the Hubble and James Webb telescopes [c49]. NASA administrator Nicky Fox expects the telescope to find tens of thousands or up to 100,000 exoplanets [c51]. Its primary survey will cover more than 2 billion galaxies over more than one year [c56]. The mission has a five-year primary lifespan and could run for 10 years [c53].

vocab.meaning: planets that orbit a star outside our solar system
the vertical takeoff of a rocket or spacecraft

stories.headline: Google Maps updates Lake Ontario name to Lake America for US users
stories.body:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America [c58]. Google updated Google Maps to show Lake America to users inside the United States [c59]. Canadian users still see Lake Ontario, while users outside both countries see both names [c64]. Apple Maps continued showing Lake Ontario to US users on August 30 [c65]. Trump previously renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America in January 2025 [c67].

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the new name [c60]. Carney said Ontario comes from a 400-year-old Wendat word meaning the lake is beautiful and great [c60]. Wendat Nation Grand Chief Pierre Picard said the order attempts to erase Indigenous history [c62]. Ontario Premier Doug Ford put up a billboard near Grimsby reading Lake Ontario Now and Always [c61]. Ford called the order something out of Saturday Night Live [c66]. New York Governor Kathy Hochul said New York State will not adopt the name [c69]. The dispute happens during a trade fight, after the US put a 50% tariff on Canadian steel [c63]. Carney walked away from trade talks on August 21 [c68].

vocab.meaning: relating to issuing orders or running a government

stories.headline: Passenger ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus leaving eight dead
stories.body:
At least eight people died after a passenger ferry capsized off northern Cyprus on Sunday evening [c70, c73]. More than a dozen people remain missing [c70]. Prime Minister Ünal Üstel said the high-speed Filo Jet ferry carried 259 passengers and eight crew members [c71, c73]. Survivor Efe Multici said the vessel hit the water violently before the front left side opened [c77]. Water quickly flooded inside the ship [c77].

The 40-meter ferry sank to a depth of 514 meters about 4 nautical miles off the coast [c73, c76]. Civilian captain Mustafa Koc rescued about 65 passengers from the water [c74]. Üstel told Turkish broadcaster TRT that 237 people were rescued and 18 remained missing [c75]. Livemint reported that 241 people were rescued [c79]. The Turkish ambassador originally reported 172 rescued and 89 missing [c78]. Turkey deployed six navy ships, five coast guard vessels, and two helicopters [c80]. Authorities detained the captain and seven crew members during an investigation [c72].

vocab.meaning: held in custody by legal authority

stories.headline: India and Uzbekistan form partnership and sign uranium pact
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi met President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent to upgrade India-Uzbekistan relations [c81]. The two leaders upgraded bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership [c81]. Modi arrived in Tashkent on August 29, 2026, for a two-day state visit [c96]. Uzbekistan was the first stop on a two-nation tour that includes a visit to Kyrgyzstan for the SCO Summit [c91].

Modi announced a long-term deal for Uzbekistan to supply uranium to India [c83]. External affairs ministry official Sibi George said both countries are close to signing the agreement [c92]. President Mirziyoyev announced a 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens [c93]. NPCI International Payments signed an agreement to let Indian UPI apps scan QR codes in Uzbekistan [c95]. The agreement was signed with Uzbekistan's National Interbank Processing Centre JSC [c95]. India also announced a $1 million grant for afforestation initiatives near the Aral Sea [c94].

India and Uzbekistan set a target of $5 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2030 [c82]. Current annual trade between the two countries stands at $1.32 billion [c86]. Indian commerce ministry data shows trade reached $1.3 billion in 2025 [c89]. That figure marked a 33.3% increase from the previous year [c89]. Uzbekistan thanked India for supporting its push to join the World Trade Organization [c90].

The two countries established a foreign minister-level coordination council to direct cooperation [c84]. Officials signed 11 agreements covering culture, education, mining, Ayurveda, tourism, and Buddhist site restoration [c85]. On August 30, 2026, President Mirziyoyev gave Modi Uzbekistan's Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order [c87]. The award is the 36th honorary award Modi has received since 2016 [c88].

vocab.meaning: the act of planting trees to establish a forest where none existed before
a formal arrangement to work together

stories.headline: Cockroach Janta Party movement gains momentum as school audits expand
stories.body:
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said organizers of the Cockroach Janta Party movement appear to have political ambitions [c97]. Wangchuk called those ambitions normal during a podcast interview [c97]. He advised organizers to stay apolitical as a pressure group to keep trust [c98]. CJP protests previously caused former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign [c99]. The movement launched volunteer audits of government schools on August 15 to check basic facilities [c105]. It set a goal to audit 100 rural schools in two months [c106].

Government data shows India has over one million state schools [c107]. Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan objected to audits done without permission [c108]. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered school checks and police cases over misleading videos [c109]. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for calling protesting youth Dimagi Naxal [c104]. Dipke also said the BJP believes it is bigger than the RSS [c102]. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated in New York that a Hindu who opposes Muslims is not a Hindu [c103]. The CJP announced a protest march in Delhi on September 5 [c111]. Retired police officer Rajendra Singh asked the Supreme Court to restrict unpermitted marches before the BRICS Summit [c110, c112]. The 1979 Assam student movement led by AASU eventually formed a government in 1985 [c100]. In 2026, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party led by C. Joseph Vijay formed the government in Tamil Nadu [c101].

vocab.meaning: public protesting or campaigning to achieve a goal
a formal written request made to an official body or court
